name: mla_prefill_varlen_lse_prefix_no_causal_n_heads12_qk_head_dim192_v_head_dim128
description: mla_prefill_varlen that also returns each query's log-sum-exp, the passes of a chunked prefix that sglang merges: sequence s's queries are q's rows cu_seqlens_q[s]:cu_seqlens_q[s + 1], its keys and values the rows cu_seqlens_k[s]:cu_seqlens_k[s + 1] of k and v (with no prefix, the queries' own rows). With causal, aligned at the end: query i of a sequence of Lq queries over Lk keys reads keys 0 .. Lk - Lq + i; without, every key of its sequence (a prefix chunk, each of whose keys precedes every query). Logits q . k * sm_scale over qk_head_dim; output the softmax-weighted sum of v, lse the natural log of the sum of exp(logit) over the keys read, per query row and head. With qkv_fp8 a kernel may round q, k and v to float8_e4m3fn first, as aiter's fp8 prefill does.

n_q.description: Query rows, every sequence's back to back.

n_kv.description: Key and value rows, every sequence's back to back.

n_heads.description: Heads on this rank; k and v carry q's.

qk_head_dim.description: Values per q and k head: the no-rope and rope parts.

v_head_dim.description: Values per v and output head.

cu_seqlens_q.description: Where each sequence's queries start in q, then where the last ends.

cu_seqlens_k.description: Where each sequence's keys start in k and v, then where the last ends.

output.description: The softmax-weighted sum of the values each query reads.

lse.description: Natural log-sum-exp of the scaled logits each query reads, [query row, head].

sources.content:
"""MLA prefill attention that also returns each query's log-sum-exp (sglang's chunked-prefix passes: the causal pass
over the extend tokens, and the pass over a prefix chunk that every query reads whole; causal over a prefix too), in
fp8: q, k and v are rounded to float8_e4m3fn (one FlyDSL launch for all three) and aiter's persistent ASM prefill
runs at the native 12 heads, causal or not, on the work plan aiter's planner builds with need_lse, built here once
per shape (``ps_plan.py``, so that aiter without need_lse serves too; a single sequence's offsets are fixed by the
row counts), so that every query tile, split or not, leaves fp32 partials with their log-sum-exp; the CU lists are
permuted so each 3-head cluster sits on two XCDs. No ASM call reads more than 65536 keys: a longer key range is cut
into segments, each its own call (causal: the prefix before the queries' own keys in segments read whole, then each
65536-query block reads its own keys' segments before it whole and its own causally). A FlyDSL kernel merges each
query tile's partials, from every segment, in a fixed order into the output and writes the tile's natural-log lse.
One sequence: dispatch serves only the sequence count the workloads measure."""

import functools
import math

import flydsl.compiler as flyc
import flydsl.expr as fx
import torch
from flydsl.expr import rocdl
from flydsl.expr.typing import T

N_HEADS = 12
QK_DIM = 192
V_DIM = 128
TILE_Q = 256  # the plan's query tile
N_CU = 256

# --- FlyDSL map reduce. Each query tile s has a descriptor row [out_base, n_rows, n_splits, p_0 .. p_{MS-1}] with
# out_base = q_start * H, n_rows = (q_end - q_start) * H and p_j = partial row j * H (padded with p_0). Row x of the
# tile (x = local_q * H + h) merges partial rows p_j + x by their natural-log lse, in j order, into out_base + x, and
# writes the merged lse, max + ln(sum of exp(lse_j - max)), to lse row out_base + x.
_LOG2E = math.log2(math.e)
_LN2 = math.log(2.0)
VEC = 4  # fp32 values per lane: one 16-byte load
LANES_PER_ROW = V_DIM // VEC
NUM_THREADS = 256
ROWS_PER_BLOCK = NUM_THREADS // LANES_PER_ROW
DESC_HEAD = 3


def _view(ptr, dtype, shape, stride):
    return fx.rocdl.make_buffer_tensor(fx.make_view(fx.recast_iter(dtype, ptr), fx.make_layout(shape, stride)))


@functools.cache
def compile_reduce(max_splits: int, short_splits: int = 0):
    """Tiles with at most short_splits splits take an unroll of that depth, the others one of max_splits."""
    MS = max_splits
    STRIDE = DESC_HEAD + MS

    @flyc.kernel(known_block_size=[NUM_THREADS, 1, 1])
    def reduce_kernel(
        part: fx.Pointer,  # f32 [P, V_DIM] (P = partial rows * H)
        lse: fx.Pointer,  # f32 [P]
        desc: fx.Pointer,  # i32 [n_tiles, STRIDE]
        out: fx.Pointer,  # bf16 [R, V_DIM]
        out_lse: fx.Pointer,  # f32 [R]
        n_part: fx.Int32,
        n_out: fx.Int32,
        n_tiles: fx.Int32,
    ):
        tid = fx.thread_idx.x
        bx = fx.block_idx.x
        by = fx.block_idx.y
        c_lanes = fx.Int32(LANES_PER_ROW)
        x = bx * fx.Int32(ROWS_PER_BLOCK) + tid // c_lanes
        lane = tid % c_lanes

        g_desc = _view(desc, fx.Int32, (n_tiles * fx.Int32(STRIDE),), (1,))
        g_part = _view(part, fx.Float32, (n_part, V_DIM), (V_DIM, 1))
        g_lse = _view(lse, fx.Float32, (n_part,), (1,))
        g_out = _view(out, fx.BFloat16, (n_out, V_DIM), (V_DIM, 1))
        r_lse = rocdl.get_buffer_rsrc(rocdl.make_buffer_ptr(out_lse, n_out * fx.Int32(4)))

        base = by * fx.Int32(STRIDE)
        out_base = g_desc[base]
        n_rows = g_desc[base + fx.Int32(1)]
        n_splits = g_desc[base + fx.Int32(2)]
        last = n_rows - fx.Int32(1)
        # a row past the tile reads the tile's last (in bounds) and stores nothing
        active = x <= last
        x = (x > last).select(last, x)

        reg_layout = fx.make_layout(VEC, 1)
        atom = fx.make_copy_atom(fx.rocdl.BufferCopy128b(), fx.Float32)
        neg_inf = fx.Float32(float("-inf"))

        def body(ms):
            lses = []
            parts = []
            for j in fx.range_constexpr(ms):
                prow = g_desc[base + fx.Int32(DESC_HEAD + j)] + x
                l = g_lse[prow]
                if j >= 1:  # an unsplit tile pads its one partial: weigh the copies 0
                    l = (fx.Int32(j) < n_splits).select(l, neg_inf)
                lses.append(l)
                tiled = fx.logical_divide(fx.slice(g_part, (prow, None)), reg_layout)
                frag = fx.make_rmem_tensor(reg_layout, fx.Float32)
                fx.copy_atom_call(atom, fx.slice(tiled, (None, lane)), frag)
                parts.append(frag.load())

            m = lses[0]
            for j in fx.range_constexpr(1, ms):
                m = m.maximumf(lses[j])
            zero = fx.Float32(0.0)
            finite = m > neg_inf
            m = finite.select(m, zero)

            acc = [zero for _ in fx.range_constexpr(VEC)]
            den = zero
            for j in fx.range_constexpr(ms):
                w = fx.Float32(fx.rocdl.exp2(T.f32, ((lses[j] - m) * _LOG2E).ir_value()))
                den = den + w
                v = parts[j]
                acc = [acc[i] + w * v[i] for i in fx.range_constexpr(VEC)]
            inv = fx.Float32((den > zero).select(fx.rocdl.rcp(T.f32, den.ir_value()), zero))

            res = fx.make_rmem_tensor(reg_layout, fx.BFloat16)
            res.store(fx.Vector.from_elements([(acc[i] * inv).to(fx.BFloat16) for i in fx.range_constexpr(VEC)],
                                              dtype=fx.BFloat16))
            out_atom = fx.make_copy_atom(fx.rocdl.BufferCopy64b(), fx.BFloat16)
            out_tiled = fx.logical_divide(fx.slice(g_out, (out_base + x, None)), reg_layout)
            # log2(0) = -inf leaves a row that read no key at -inf
            row_lse = m + fx.Float32(fx.rocdl.log(T.f32, den.ir_value())) * _LN2
            if active:
                fx.copy_atom_call(out_atom, res, fx.slice(out_tiled, (None, lane)))
                # the row's first lane stores its lse
                if lane == fx.Int32(0):
                    rocdl.raw_ptr_buffer_store(
                        row_lse.ir_value(), r_lse, ((out_base + x) * fx.Int32(4)).ir_value(), fx.Int32(0).ir_value()
                    )

        if 0 < short_splits < MS:
            if n_splits <= fx.Int32(short_splits):
                body(short_splits)
            else:
                body(MS)
        else:
            body(MS)

    @flyc.jit
    def launch(
        part: fx.Pointer,
        lse: fx.Pointer,
        desc: fx.Pointer,
        out: fx.Pointer,
        out_lse: fx.Pointer,
        n_part: fx.Int32,
        n_out: fx.Int32,
        n_tiles: fx.Int32,
        n_blocks: fx.Int32,
        stream: fx.Stream = fx.Stream(None),
    ):
        reduce_kernel(part, lse, desc, out, out_lse, n_part, n_out, n_tiles).launch(
            grid=(n_blocks, n_tiles, 1), block=(NUM_THREADS, 1, 1), stream=stream
        )

    return launch

# --- FlyDSL fused bf16 -> fp8 e4m3fn cast of q, k and v in one launch. Each tensor is a flat run of 8-element rows;
# block b owns unroll x 256 consecutive rows of one tensor (the blocks of q come first, then k, then v), each
# lane one 16-byte nontemporal bf16 load and one 8-byte fp8 store per step. The buffers' sizes bound the tails.
CAST_THREADS = 256
CAST_VEC = 8
# Rows per lane, and the loads' cache policy: the bf16 inputs are read once, so they load nontemporal (slc) and leave
# the caches to the fp8 outputs the ASM reads next; the stores keep the default policy (nontemporal stores make the
# cast alone 19 % faster on 893/35107 but the ASM slower by more). Measured on cast + ASM + reduce in CUDA graphs:
# nontemporal loads at unroll 2 against default loads at unroll 1-2: 893/35107 -1.2 %, 2732/35107 -0.6 %,
# 2732/104093 -1.8 %, 9397/104093 -0.5 %, 16384/65536 -0.5 %, 16384/131072 -0.4 %; unroll 2 beats 1, 3 and 4 there.
CAST_UNROLL = 2
CAST_LOAD_POLICY = 2  # slc: nontemporal


def _flat_view(ptr, dtype, n_rows, width):
    t = fx.make_view(fx.recast_iter(dtype, ptr), fx.make_layout((n_rows, width), (width, 1)))
    return fx.rocdl.make_buffer_tensor(t, max_size=False)


@functools.cache
def compile_cast(unroll: int):
    rows_per_block = CAST_THREADS * unroll
    @flyc.kernel(known_block_size=[CAST_THREADS, 1, 1])
    def cast_kernel(
        q: fx.Pointer, k: fx.Pointer, v: fx.Pointer,  # bf16
        qo: fx.Pointer, ko: fx.Pointer, vo: fx.Pointer,  # fp8 bytes, as i32 pairs
        nq: fx.Int32, nk: fx.Int32, nv: fx.Int32,  # 8-element rows
        bq: fx.Int32, bk: fx.Int32,  # blocks of q, of q and k
    ):  # fmt: skip
        tid = fx.thread_idx.x
        bx = fx.block_idx.x
        reg_in = fx.make_layout(CAST_VEC, 1)
        reg_out = fx.make_layout(2, 1)
        atom_in = fx.make_copy_atom(fx.rocdl.BufferCopy128b(CAST_LOAD_POLICY), fx.BFloat16)
        atom_out = fx.make_copy_atom(fx.rocdl.BufferCopy64b(), fx.Int32)

        def body(src, dst, n, b):
            g_in = _flat_view(src, fx.BFloat16, n, CAST_VEC)
            g_out = _flat_view(dst, fx.Int32, n, 2)
            row0 = b * fx.Int32(rows_per_block) + tid
            vals = []
            for u in fx.range_constexpr(unroll):
                row = row0 + fx.Int32(u * CAST_THREADS)
                frag = fx.make_rmem_tensor(reg_in, fx.BFloat16)
                fx.copy_atom_call(atom_in, fx.slice(g_in, (row, None)), frag)
                vals.append(frag.load())
            for u in fx.range_constexpr(unroll):
                row = row0 + fx.Int32(u * CAST_THREADS)
                x = vals[u]
                f = [x[i].to(fx.Float32) for i in fx.range_constexpr(CAST_VEC)]
                words = []
                for w in fx.range_constexpr(2):
                    lo = fx.rocdl.cvt_pk_fp8_f32(T.i32, f[4 * w].ir_value(), f[4 * w + 1].ir_value(),
                                                  fx.Int32(0).ir_value(), False)
                    hi = fx.rocdl.cvt_pk_fp8_f32(T.i32, f[4 * w + 2].ir_value(), f[4 * w + 3].ir_value(),
                                                  lo, True)
                    words.append(fx.Int32(hi))
                res = fx.make_rmem_tensor(reg_out, fx.Int32)
                res.store(fx.Vector.from_elements(words, dtype=fx.Int32))
                fx.copy_atom_call(atom_out, res, fx.slice(g_out, (row, None)))

        if bx < bq:
            body(q, qo, nq, bx)
        elif bx < bk:
            body(k, ko, nk, bx - bq)
        else:
            body(v, vo, nv, bx - bk)

    @flyc.jit
    def launch(
        q: fx.Pointer, k: fx.Pointer, v: fx.Pointer,
        qo: fx.Pointer, ko: fx.Pointer, vo: fx.Pointer,
        nq: fx.Int32, nk: fx.Int32, nv: fx.Int32,
        bq: fx.Int32, bk: fx.Int32, n_blocks: fx.Int32,
        stream: fx.Stream = fx.Stream(None),
    ):  # fmt: skip
        assert unroll >= 1  # the unroll is a closure int the launcher reads, so it is part of the cache key
        cast_kernel(q, k, v, qo, ko, vo, nq, nk, nv, bq, bk).launch(
            grid=(n_blocks, 1, 1), block=(CAST_THREADS, 1, 1), stream=stream
        )

    return launch


# CAST_VEC-wide rows one launch converts of each tensor: their byte offsets stay within int32 (2**26 rows are 1 GiB
# of bf16)
CAST_MAX_ROWS = 1 << 26


def cast_fp8(q, k, v, qf, kf, vf, unroll: int):
    """q, k, v (contiguous bf16) -> qf, kf, vf (contiguous fp8 e4m3fn) in one launch, one per CAST_MAX_ROWS rows of
    the largest past that."""
    counts = [x.numel() // CAST_VEC for x in (q, k, v)]
    rows = CAST_THREADS * unroll
    cb = lambda n: (n + rows - 1) // rows  # noqa: E731
    stream = fx.Stream(torch.cuda.current_stream(q.device))
    for r0 in range(0, max(counts), CAST_MAX_ROWS):
        nq, nk, nv = (min(max(n - r0, 0), CAST_MAX_ROWS) for n in counts)
        bq, bk, bv = cb(nq), cb(nk), cb(nv)
        src = [x.data_ptr() + r0 * CAST_VEC * 2 for x in (q, k, v)]
        dst = [x.data_ptr() + r0 * CAST_VEC for x in (qf, kf, vf)]
        compile_cast(unroll)(
            *(flyc.from_c_void_p(fx.BFloat16, p) for p in src), *(flyc.from_c_void_p(fx.Int32, p) for p in dst),
            nq, nk, nv, bq, bq + bk, bq + bk + bv, stream,
        )  # fmt: skip


def _d1a(work_indptr, work_info):
    """Permute aiter's whole CU lists so each 3-head cluster sits on two XCDs (WG w runs on XCD w % 8)."""
    wi = work_indptr.tolist()
    info = work_info.view(-1, 8).tolist()
    n = len(wi) - 1
    clusters = {}
    for l in range(n):
        cs = {(info[w][7] & 0xFFFF) // 3 for w in range(wi[l], wi[l + 1])}
        if len(cs) != 1:
            return work_indptr, work_info
        clusters.setdefault(cs.pop(), []).append(l)
    if n != N_CU or len(clusters) != 4 or any(len(v) != 64 for v in clusters.values()):
        return work_indptr, work_info
    new = [None] * n
    for c, ls in clusters.items():
        for i, l in enumerate(ls):
            new[(i // 2) * 8 + 2 * c + (i % 2)] = info[wi[l] : wi[l + 1]]
    indptr, flat = [0], []
    for lst in new:
        for it in lst:
            flat += it
        indptr.append(indptr[-1] + len(lst))
    rest = work_info.view(-1)[len(flat):].tolist()
    dev = work_info.device
    return (torch.tensor(indptr, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev),
            torch.tensor(flat + rest, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev).view(work_info.shape))


# Most keys one ASM call reads: longer key ranges are cut into segments of this many, each its own call, and the
# reduce merges every segment's partials by their lse.
KV_SEGMENT = 65536
# plans kept per shape: a forward's layers share one, and serving sees new lengths without end
PLANS_KEPT = 64


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=PLANS_KEPT)
def _piece_plan(n_q: int, n_kv: int, causal: bool, device):
    """aiter's persistent plan with need_lse for n_q queries over n_kv keys (one sequence), its CU lists permuted,
    the piece's offsets, and per query tile (q_start, q_end, its partial rows in split order).

    The plan is built on the host and copied in stream order (aiter's own planner writes its device buffers with a
    synchronous hipMemcpy on the null stream, which does not order with the current torch stream)."""
    from .ps_plan import ps_plan

    work_indptr, works, indptr, final, partial = ps_plan(
        [0, n_q], [0, n_kv], [n_kv], N_HEADS, num_cus=N_CU, qlen_granularity=TILE_Q, kvlen_granularity=128,
        block_size=1, is_causal=causal,
    )  # fmt: skip
    work_indptr, work_info = _d1a(torch.tensor(work_indptr, dtype=torch.int32), torch.tensor(works, dtype=torch.int32))
    # in stream order, from pageable host memory: the copy has read it once it returns
    work_indptr, work_info = work_indptr.to(device), work_info.to(device)
    tiles = [(*final[t], partial[indptr[t] : indptr[t + 1]]) for t in range(len(final))]
    n_partial = max(r for _, _, rows in tiles for r in rows) + TILE_Q
    offsets_q = torch.tensor([0, n_q], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    offsets_k = torch.tensor([0, n_kv], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    indices = torch.arange(n_kv, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    return work_indptr, work_info, offsets_q, offsets_k, indices, n_partial, tiles


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=PLANS_KEPT)
def _plan(n_q: int, n_kv: int, causal: bool, device):
    """The ASM calls over one sequence, none reading more than KV_SEGMENT keys, and the reduce over all of them.
    Without the causal mask every query reads key segments [s, s + KV_SEGMENT); with it, the n_kv - n_q prefix keys
    before the queries' own are read whole in such segments, and query block [j, j + KV_SEGMENT) reads its own keys'
    segments before it whole and its own causally."""
    pieces = []
    if causal:
        prefix = n_kv - n_q
        pieces = [(0, n_q, i, min(i + KV_SEGMENT, prefix), False) for i in range(0, prefix, KV_SEGMENT)]
        for j in range(0, n_q, KV_SEGMENT):
            q_end = min(j + KV_SEGMENT, n_q)
            pieces += [(j, q_end, prefix + i, prefix + i + KV_SEGMENT, False) for i in range(0, j, KV_SEGMENT)]
            pieces.append((j, q_end, prefix + j, prefix + q_end, True))
    else:
        pieces = [(0, n_q, i, min(i + KV_SEGMENT, n_kv), False) for i in range(0, n_kv, KV_SEGMENT)]
    calls, groups, base = [], {}, 0
    for q0, q1, k0, k1, piece_causal in pieces:
        work_indptr, work_info, offsets_q, offsets_k, indices, n_partial, tiles = _piece_plan(
            q1 - q0, k1 - k0, piece_causal, device
        )
        for q_start, q_end, rows in tiles:
            groups.setdefault((q0 + q_start, q0 + q_end), []).extend(base + r for r in rows)
        calls.append((q0, q1, k0, k1, piece_causal, work_indptr, work_info, offsets_q, offsets_k, indices, base,
                      n_partial))  # fmt: skip
        base += n_partial
    spans = sorted(groups)
    # every query row reduced exactly once
    assert spans[0][0] == 0 and spans[-1][1] == n_q and all(a[1] == b[0] for a, b in zip(spans, spans[1:]))
    max_splits = max(len(rows) for rows in groups.values())
    desc = []
    for q_start, q_end in spans:
        ps = [r * N_HEADS for r in groups[(q_start, q_end)]]
        ps += [ps[0]] * (max_splits - len(ps))
        desc += [q_start * N_HEADS, (q_end - q_start) * N_HEADS, len(groups[(q_start, q_end)])] + ps
    # tiles split less deeply than the deepest take their own unroll: the one that minimises the loads summed over
    # tiles, when it saves at least 15 % of them
    counts = [len(rows) for rows in groups.values()]
    cost = lambda sh: sum(sh if n <= sh else max_splits for n in counts) if sh else max_splits * len(counts)  # noqa: E731
    short = min(sorted({n for n in counts if n < max_splits}), key=lambda sh: (cost(sh), sh), default=0)
    short = short if short and cost(short) <= 0.85 * cost(0) else 0
    desc_t = torch.tensor(desc, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    one = torch.ones((), dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    return tuple(calls), one, base, desc_t, len(spans), compile_reduce(max_splits, short)


def run(*, q, k, v, cu_seqlens_q, qkv_fp8, causal, cu_seqlens_k, sm_scale, output, lse):
    # one sequence (the workloads' sequence count), whose offsets the row counts fix
    n_q, n_kv = q.shape[0], k.shape[0]
    from aiter import mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd

    calls, one, n_partial, desc, n_tiles, launch = _plan(n_q, n_kv, causal, q.device)
    fp8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn
    if q.is_contiguous() and k.is_contiguous() and v.is_contiguous():
        nq, nk = q.numel(), k.numel()
        buf = torch.empty(nq + nk + v.numel(), dtype=fp8, device=q.device)
        qf, kf, vf = buf[:nq].view(q.shape), buf[nq : nq + nk].view(k.shape), buf[nq + nk :].view(v.shape)
        cast_fp8(q, k, v, qf, kf, vf, CAST_UNROLL)
    else:
        qf, kf, vf = q.to(fp8), k.to(fp8), v.to(fp8)
    logits = torch.empty((n_partial, N_HEADS, V_DIM), dtype=torch.float32, device=q.device)
    part_lse = torch.empty((n_partial, N_HEADS), dtype=torch.float32, device=q.device)
    for q0, q1, k0, k1, piece_causal, work_indptr, work_info, offsets_q, offsets_kv, indices, base, rows in calls:
        mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd(
            qf[q0:q1], kf[k0:k1], vf[k0:k1], offsets_q, offsets_kv, indices, work_indptr, work_info, q1 - q0,
            sm_scale, piece_causal, logits[base : base + rows], part_lse[base : base + rows], output[q0:q1],
            one, one, one,
        )  # fmt: skip
    launch(
        flyc.from_c_void_p(fx.Float32, logits.data_ptr()),
        flyc.from_c_void_p(fx.Float32, part_lse.data_ptr()),
        flyc.from_c_void_p(fx.Int32, desc.data_ptr()),
        flyc.from_c_void_p(fx.BFloat16, output.data_ptr()),
        flyc.from_c_void_p(fx.Float32, lse.data_ptr()),
        n_partial * N_HEADS,
        n_q * N_HEADS,
        n_tiles,
        (TILE_Q * N_HEADS) // ROWS_PER_BLOCK,
        fx.Stream(torch.cuda.current_stream(output.device)),
    )

"""aiter's persistent plan for its fp8 MLA prefill as ``get_ps_metadata_v1(..., need_lse=True)`` builds it
(``csrc/kernels/mla/metadata/v1_2_host.cuh``), in Python: every query tile, split over CUs or not, leaves fp32
partials with their log-sum-exp for the reduce. aiter's planner takes ``need_lse`` from 0.1.23 on; older ones (the
one in sglang 0.5.22's image) leave a tile one CU reads whole unreduced, so its lse is never written."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math


def _ceil_div(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    """C's ``(a + b - 1) / b``, which truncates toward zero."""
    n = a + b - 1
    return n // b if n >= 0 else -(-n // b)


def ps_plan(
    qo_indptr: list[int],
    kv_indptr: list[int],
    kv_lens: list[int],
    num_heads_k: int,
    *,
    num_cus: int,
    qlen_granularity: int = 256,
    kvlen_granularity: int = 128,
    block_size: int = 1,
    is_causal: bool = True,
) -> tuple[list[int], list[list[int]], list[int], list[list[int]], list[int]]:
    """``(work_indptr, work_info, reduce_indptr, reduce_final_map, reduce_partial_map)`` as lists, as aiter's planner
    fills them with ``need_lse`` and one query head per key head (only its used rows: ``num_cus + 1``, one
    ``[batch, partial_qo_loc, qo_start, qo_end, kv_start, kv_end, kv_offset, q_head_range]`` per work, one entry per
    query tile), for sequences at ``qo_indptr``'s query rows over ``kv_indptr``'s key blocks, ``kv_lens`` keys each."""
    clusters = math.gcd(num_heads_k, num_cus)
    tgs = num_cus // clusters
    heads = num_heads_k // clusters
    per_unit = kvlen_granularity // block_size

    # each sequence's query tiles, head and tail alternately (0, n-1, 1, n-2, ...), with the key blocks they read
    tiles, units = [], 0
    for b in range(len(qo_indptr) - 1):
        qo_len, kv_len = qo_indptr[b + 1] - qo_indptr[b], kv_lens[b]
        ranges = [(s, min(s + qlen_granularity, qo_len)) for s in range(0, qo_len, qlen_granularity)]
        for i in range(len(ranges)):
            start, end = ranges[i // 2 if i % 2 == 0 else len(ranges) - 1 - i // 2]
            kv = min(kv_len - qo_len + end, kv_len) if is_causal else kv_len
            n = _ceil_div(kv, kvlen_granularity)
            tiles.append((b, start + qo_indptr[b], end + qo_indptr[b], n * per_unit, kv))
            units += n
    average, remainder = units // tgs, units % tgs

    work_indptr, works = [0] * (num_cus + 1), []
    for cluster in range(clusters):
        # each CU of the cluster takes its share of key blocks, the same for every head of the cluster
        tile = block = partial = 0
        for tg in range(tgs):
            for h in range(heads):
                head = cluster * heads + h
                head_range = ((head + 1) << 16) | (head & 0xFFFF)
                saved = (tile, block, partial)
                capacity = (average + 1 if tg < remainder else average) * per_unit
                while tile < len(tiles) and capacity > 0:
                    b, qo_start, qo_end, n_blocks, kv = tiles[tile]
                    kv_start = block + kv_indptr[b]
                    if kv - block * block_size <= capacity * block_size:
                        # the rest of the tile; reduced even when whole (need_lse), unless it reads nothing
                        consumed = n_blocks - block
                        loc = -1 if consumed == 0 else qlen_granularity * partial
                        partial += consumed != 0
                        kv_end = min(kv_start + consumed, kv_indptr[b + 1])
                        works.append([b, loc, qo_start, qo_end, kv_start, kv_end, 0, head_range])
                        tile, block = tile + 1, 0
                    else:
                        consumed = capacity
                        kv_end = min(kv_start + consumed, kv_indptr[b + 1])
                        kv_offset = kv_lens[b] - (kv_end - kv_indptr[b]) * block_size
                        works.append([b, qlen_granularity * partial, qo_start, qo_end, kv_start, kv_end, kv_offset, head_range])  # fmt: skip
                        partial += 1
                        block += consumed
                    capacity -= consumed
                if h != heads - 1:
                    tile, block, partial = saved
            work_indptr[cluster * tgs + tg + 1] = len(works)

    # one reduce per query tile, its partials in ascending order; every query row in exactly one
    groups: dict[tuple[int, int], set[int]] = {}
    for w in works:
        if w[1] != -1:
            groups.setdefault((w[2], w[3]), set()).add(w[1])
    reduce_indptr, final, partials, covered = [0], [], [], 0
    for start, end in sorted(groups):
        if start != covered:
            raise ValueError(
                f"query rows [{covered}, {start}) are in no reduce: their lse would be unwritten"
            )
        covered = end
        partials += sorted(groups[(start, end)])
        reduce_indptr.append(len(partials))
        final.append([start, end])
    if covered != qo_indptr[-1]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"query rows [{covered}, {qo_indptr[-1]}) are in no reduce: their lse would be unwritten"
        )
    return work_indptr, works, reduce_indptr, final, partials
